monthly_review.summary: Running volume collapsed by 82% from September to October, pace improved slightly but on drastically reduced intensity exposure, and efficiency metrics plateaued without supporting aerobic load.
monthly_review.highlight: Efficiency worsened (+0.50 ml/kg/km) despite faster average pace and higher cadence — a red flag that recent running economy is deteriorating under low-load conditions, inconsistent with true fitness gain and suggestive of residual fatigue or deconditioning.

goal_tracker.message: Matching last month would require 64.1 km across 12 sessions in 28 days — an unsustainable 2.3 km/session average, especially given compromised readiness. Chasing this number is inadvisable and risks injury or burnout; recovery must take priority over volume targets.

insights.title: Worsening running economy despite faster pace
insights.body: Efficiency declined from 14.58 to 15.08 ml/kg/km while avg pace improved — this inverse relationship suggests neuromuscular inefficiency or gait compensation, not genuine aerobic improvement; notably, vertical oscill held steady (8.1–8.6) but ground contact time dropped from ~306 ms (Sep) to ~302 ms (Oct), possibly reflecting rushed, less controlled strides.

insights.title: Collapse in Zone 4 exposure
insights.body: Zone 4 dropped from 20% of total time in Sep to just 9% in Oct, while Zone 2 remained dominant (44%). This isn’t periodised deload — it’s a near-elimination of threshold stimulus, yet VO2max remains stable at 41.0, implying stagnation rather than preservation.

insights.title: Cadence rose without efficiency gain
insights.body: Cadence increased +8 spm (146 → 154) but efficiency worsened — typically, higher cadence improves economy *only* when paired with reduced vertical oscill and ground contact time; here, vertical oscill increased slightly (8.1→8.4) and ground contact time decreased minimally, indicating inefficient turnover.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling unchanged despite load drop
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE held at 2.9 across both months, even though total volume and Zone 4 work plummeted — this stability masks loss of aerobic resilience, as decoupling only reveals strain when challenged; absence of stress means the metric is uninformative, not reassuring.

recommendations.action: Complete 3x 45-min Zone 1 runs (HR ≤125 bpm) on Mon/Wed/Fri, no pace target — focus on relaxed breathing and arm swing symmetry
recommendations.reason: Zone 1 preserves aerobic base with minimal autonomic demand, aligning with compromised readiness and allowing HRV re-establishment

recommendations.action: Perform daily 10-min guided HRV biofeedback (e.g., breathwork at 5.5 breaths/min) with Garmin Body Battery tracking before and after
recommendations.reason: Body Battery and HRV are missing from dataset but are essential for quantifying recovery; this builds objective input for next review

recommendations.action: Skip all Zone 3+ efforts for 7 days; replace any planned tempo or intervals with walk-run strides (30 sec jog / 90 sec walk × 6) at perceived exertion ≤3/10
recommendations.reason: Zone 4 collapse and efficiency decline indicate insufficient recovery to handle metabolic or neuromuscular stress — reintroducing intensity now risks reinforcing poor movement patterns

risk_flags.evidence: Efficiency worsening (+0.50 ml/kg/km) despite stable VO2max (41.0) and reduced Zone 4 exposure (20% → 9%)
risk_flags.action: Restore Zone 4 volume gradually over 3 weeks, starting with 2×8 min @ Z4 HR, not pace

risk_flags.evidence: Pace improved (+26 sec/km) while efficiency declined and cadence rose abnormally (+8 spm) without stride length or vertical oscillillation improvement
risk_flags.action: Add 2x weekly barefoot drills on grass (e.g., A-skips, straight-leg bounds) to recalibrate proprioception and stride timing

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish autonomic regulation, rebuild neuromuscular coordination, and restore confidence in effortless movement — not speed, distance, or zones.
suggested_sessions: Walk-run strides with form focus (30s jog / 90s walk × 6)
